name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.exists_character_annihilating_closedIdeal_of_not_mem
title: A character separating a closed ideal

content.display_title: A character separating a closed ideal
content.one_sentence_role: Finds one character which kills a closed ideal and detects a specified element outside it.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $D$ be a commutative unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $J$ be a norm-closed ideal, and let $d\in D\setminus J$. There is a character $\chi:D\to\mathbb C$ such that $$\chi(x)=0\quad(x\in J),\qquad \chi(d)\ne0.$$ A character here is a nonzero complex algebra homomorphism, hence unital and continuous.
content.assumptions: Closedness is for the norm topology. Properness of $J$ and nontriviality of $D$ follow from $d\notin J$; they are not extra hypotheses.
content.conclusion: The same character satisfies both annihilation of all of $J$ and nonvanishing at $d$.
content.proof_summary: Transport the ideal through the isometric Gelfand transform, find a point where the transformed element escapes its vanishing conditions, and evaluate there.
proof_steps: Let $X$ be the character space of $D$ and $G:D\to C(X,\mathbb C)$ its Gelfand $*$-isomorphism, so $G(x)(\chi)=\chi(x)$. Put $K=G(J)$. Surjectivity and multiplicativity make $K$ an ideal. Since $G$ is an isometry and a homeomorphism, $K$ is closed. If $G(d)\in K$, then $G(d)=G(x)$ for some $x\in J$, contradicting injectivity of $G$ and $d\notin J$.

Apply [The closed-ideal description applied to this Gelfand image](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/ClosedIdealCharacter.lean#L20-L65) to the norm-closed ideal $K$ of continuous functions on the compact Hausdorff $X$. It gives $$K=\{f\in C(X,\mathbb C): f|_Z=0\},\qquad Z=\{\chi\in X:g(\chi)=0\text{ for all }g\in K\}.$$ Since $G(d)\notin K$, there is $\chi\in Z$ with $G(d)(\chi)\ne0$.

For $x\in J$, the function $G(x)$ belongs to $K$, hence $\chi(x)=G(x)(\chi)=0$. At the distinguished element, $\chi(d)=G(d)(\chi)\ne0$. These are the two required conditions on the very same point $\chi$ of the character space.
